question: The world's largest population of which endangered species resides in Assam's Kaziranga National Park?
solution:
The correct answer is __**One-horned rhinoceros**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kaziranga National Park** in Assam is renowned for housing the world's largest population of the endangered **One-horned rhinoceros**.
 
• The park provides a crucial habitat for this species, playing a vital role in their conservation.
 
• As per the latest census, Kaziranga hosts more than 2,400 One-horned rhinoceroses, which is about two-thirds of their global population.
 
• The One-horned rhinoceros is also known as the Indian rhinoceros and is listed as vulnerable by the IUCN Red List.
 
• The park's efforts in anti-poaching and habitat management have significantly contributed to the increase in the rhino population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kaziranga National Park** is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its unique natural environment.
 
• Besides the One-horned rhinoceros, the park is also home to other wildlife such as tigers, elephants, and various species of birds.
 
• The park spans an area of approximately 430 square kilometers and is characterized by its tall elephant grass, marshland, and dense tropical moist broadleaf forests.
 
• Conservation efforts in Kaziranga are supported by various national and international organizations, ensuring the protection of its diverse ecosystem.
 
• The park attracts thousands of tourists annually, contributing to the local economy and raising awareness about wildlife conservation.
